name: woocommerce
note: Spike C: provenance-proposal ground truth. Spike D: full product-meta coverage, _price reclassified authored, a referential delete guard on products vs. order lookup rows, and full shop_coupon classification (see notes). Grind R1-B: variable products + variations (product_variation post type, dynamic attribute_pa_* meta via meta_patterns, _default_attributes/_product_attributes), a grouped product's _children, and _price reclassified AGAIN — this time to derived (see notes; the Spike D reasoning for 'authored' held for simple products but variable products break the engine's single-row assumption). Shipping zones and tax rates (custom tables) get typed-snapshot intent markers only, honestly: no capture/apply path exists for those tables yet (see notes and docs/grind/r1b-shop.md's acceptance criteria) — its harder 'option-name embeds another table's auto-increment id' sub-problem (shipping-method instance settings) is not attempted. Task #75: woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies GRADUATED to the real agent/src/Snapshot.php typed-snapshot grammar (natural-key identity on attribute_name) — the secondary fixture proving the same engine capability nf3_forms/nf3_fields/nf3_actions prove primarily (manifests/ninja-forms.json); see its own note below. Task #88: product_variation.title classified derived via the new per-post_type "fields" grammar (Policy::field_class()) — closes #72's self-healing post_title anomaly for real (see its own note below), the first and so far only user of this new post-FIELD (not post_meta) classification mechanism. DUO-3222 (version-pinned adapter compatibility contract) CLOSES the 'version-range pinning... lands with the plugin-manifest workstream' forward-reference this note used to end on: plugin/version_range verified live (not guessed) — woocommerce/woocommerce.php, WooCommerce 11.0.0 installed fresh from wp.org this session, landing exactly on a major-version boundary (not a coincidence worth over-reading — just where wp.org's current release happens to sit). Range scoped to the CURRENT major line only (11.x, [11.0.0, 12.0.0)) — this manifest's own HPOS/orders-table assumptions are exactly the kind of major-version-boundary-sensitive behavior DESIGN.md's own 'a manifest for Woo 7 must not claim Woo 9' example warns about, so widening to cover other major versions (backward OR forward) is DUO-3224's/DUO-3225's ratification job against real evidence, never invented here. No theme_version_range declared: confirmed empirically (sandbox/conformance/run.sh has no per-manifest theme-activation step beyond the FSE-specific block-theme setup) that no conformance seed pins a specific theme for this manifest today — Storefront is used in grind rounds (docs/grind/r1b-shop.md, r3a-multilingual-shop.md) but not the automated conformance sweep, so a theme declaration here would be exactly the untested-guess this project's discipline avoids; the theme mechanism itself is proven by a fixture (see the adapter-compatibility regression), not asserted here without a real conformance seed behind it. Task #123 (DUO-3214b): `_product_attributes` now declares `"order_preserving": true` (spec v0.15) — its top-level attribute-name keys, and every level nested inside each attribute's own row, survive capture/apply in the site's own creation order instead of being alphabetically resorted, closing the permanent (non-timing) variation-title word-reordering bug task #88's own note above flags as a separate residual. Confirmed live on two independent attribute orderings (this manifest's own r1b fixture, pa_size created before pa_color; r3a's independent fixture) with TRUE zero-exclusion byte identity, title included — no anagram carve-out needed anymore. A manifest-set audit of `_default_attributes`/`_children`/`_upsell_ids`/`_crosssell_ids` (this manifest's own most plausible siblings) found no evidence any of them need the same declaration: `_default_attributes` is looked up by key, never iterated in display order, per its own note below; the other three are plain sequential-integer PHP lists (`array_is_list()` true), which `Canon::normalize()` never sorted in the first place.

notes._low_stock_amount: Per-product low-stock threshold override reads like a runtime signal (it's stock-adjacent) but it's a merchant-set policy value, not something WooCommerce derives or recomputes — classified authored deliberately rather than lumped in with _stock/_stock_status.
notes._price: REVISED in Grind R1-B — was authored (Spike D), now derived. Spike D's reasoning still holds for SIMPLE products: _price is fully computable from _regular_price/_sale_price/_sale_price_dates_* and capturing it directly avoided a rebuilder. What Spike D never exercised is a VARIABLE product: WooCommerce's own data store (class-wc-product-variable-data-store-cpt.php's price sync) writes _price as MULTI-VALUE meta on the variable parent — one row per DISTINCT variation price, not one row for a range (confirmed empirically: a parent with variations at 19.99/19.99/18.99/21.99 carries three separate _price postmeta rows, {18.99, 19.99, 21.99} — this is how WooCommerce's own price-range catalog filter widget can do a plain meta_query on _price without a dedicated min/max column). Capture.php's authored-meta path assumes exactly one row per key and throws 'multi-value authored meta unsupported in v0' the instant it meets a second row (agent/src/Capture.php, the same guard the existing _used_by note documents for coupon redemptions) — meaning NO variable product could be captured at all while _price stayed authored, full stop, regardless of any other manifest work. Classification isn't post-type-scoped in this engine (Policy::rule() never takes a post type), so the fix has to be global: derived is semantically correct too (Spike D's own note already established _price is fully computable from other authored fields) and 'derived' meta is exempt from the multi-row check entirely (Capture.php only applies it to class === 'authored'). Empirically verified after reclassifying: the parent's price RANGE display and variation purchasability do not depend on the parent's own _price meta at all — WC_Product_Variable computes the displayed range and each variation's own effective price live from the variations' individual (single-valued) _regular_price/_sale_price/_price, which round-trip normally since a single variation only ever has one price. The parent's _price meta is a catalog-search optimization, not something product pages or Store API purchase flows read. No rebuilder was added for it (none of WooCommerce's own wp-cli-reachable commands force that specific resync; inventing one via an eval one-liner smuggled through a rebuilder's plain command string felt like exactly the 'regex-on-strings' fragility DESIGN.md warns against for a payoff that testing showed unnecessary) — if a future price-range storefront widget or CSV price-filter search is added to a grind/conformance scenario and is found to need it, that's the trigger to revisit, not a hypothetical.
notes._used_by: Every coupon redemption adds a NEW postmeta row via add_post_meta() (never update) — one row per use, value = lowercased user id or guest billing email (class-wc-coupon-data-store-cpt.php add_coupon_used_by()). This is exactly the multi-value-authored-meta shape v0's engine refuses (Capture.php throws on >1 row for an 'authored' key) — classifying it runtime is not just correct (it's redemption history, not merchant-authored config) but is what keeps capture from throwing on any coupon that's ever been used. Confirmed empirically: redeeming a coupon on env A adds a `_used_by` row and increments `usage_count`; neither must propagate to env B on apply (runtime isolation).
notes._children: Grouped product's member simple products (WC_Product_Grouped::set_children()). Confirmed empirically as a real serialized PHP array of ints keyed by sequential integer index — `a:2:{i:0;i:15;i:1;i:16;}` — not a CSV string like product_ids and not string-cast like _crosssell_ids/_upsell_ids: ref post[] with no cast, the plain int[] shape (same declared shape as product_categories, just pointing at posts instead of terms). Lint's bare_id check is exactly what catches an accidental omission of the ref declaration here — verified live during this manifest's authoring: dropping `ref: post[]` and recapturing produced two real bare_id findings naming the actual child products by title, restoring the declaration made lint clean again on the same recapture.
notes._default_attributes: Variable product's pre-selected variation, one entry per used-for-variation attribute (WC_Product_Variable::set_default_attributes()). Confirmed empirically: `a:2:{s:7:"pa_size";s:5:"small";s:8:"pa_color";s:3:"red";}` — keyed by the attribute's TAXONOMY NAME (`pa_size`, a string, stable across environments by construction) with the value being the term SLUG (also a stable string), never a term_id. Classified authored, no ref — there is no numeric id anywhere in this value to rewrite; a slug is exactly as portable as the option/meta keys that already round-trip without tokenization.
notes._product_attributes: Every product's (simple or variable) attribute assignment table (WC_Product::set_attributes(), always present once any attribute is added, even a single custom/local one). Confirmed empirically for a variable product using GLOBAL (taxonomy) attributes: `a:2:{s:7:"pa_size";a:6:{s:4:"name";s:7:"pa_size";s:5:"value";s:0:"";s:8:"position";i:0;s:10:"is_visible";i:1;s:12:"is_variation";i:1;s:11:"is_taxonomy";i:1;}...}` — `value` is the empty string for every is_taxonomy=1 entry; the actual term assignment lives in the ordinary term_relationships under the pa_* taxonomy (captured through the generic taxonomy machinery once pa_size/pa_color are in policy.taxonomies scope — see the pa_* note below), not in this meta value at all. A LOCAL (non-global, product-specific) attribute would instead put its option list directly in `value` as a pipe-separated string of free text (e.g. `Cotton | Wool`) — still no numeric ids, just prose the merchant typed. Either shape is plain, ref-free data: classified authored with no ref/json_refs declaration. (Scope note: this manifest's shop only exercises the taxonomy/global-attribute shape; the local-attribute pipe-string shape is documented here from WooCommerce's own known behavior, not independently re-verified in this round — flagged rather than silently assumed.)
notes._variation_description: Per-variation description field (WC_Product_Variation), written unconditionally on every variation create/update — even to an empty string, so it hits the classification gate on the very first variable product a site ever gets, not just ones that use it. Plain text, classified authored, no ref.
notes.product_variation.title (fields, task #8: post_title is a POST FIELD (one of the ~13 keys Capture::build_post()/Apply::finalize_post() hardcode into every post's front matter unconditionally), not post_meta/options — until task #88 there was no manifest hook to classify one at all. Root cause, confirmed via WooCommerce's own source and empirically reproduced on the r1b pair (task #72): WC_Product_Variation_Data_Store_CPT::read() recomputes a variation's title from the PARENT's _product_attributes order plus the variation's own current attribute values on EVERY wc_get_product() load, writing the result via a raw $wpdb->update() specifically to dodge wp_update_post()/save_post (WooCommerce's own code comment: avoiding an infinite loop) — hook-free, invisible to Apply's canary, no post_modified bump. Two environments that have received a different number/timing of ordinary WooCommerce-mediated reads (an admin view, a Store API request, a wc-cli command) can therefore transiently hold different title BYTES for the identical variation while every authored input (parent title, attribute assignments — both already captured/applied correctly) is byte-identical on both sides; they converge to the same self-healed value once each has had at least one such read, because the computed value depends only on that already-portable data, nothing environment-local. Declared here as {"class": "derived"} under this post_type's new "fields" key (Policy::field_class(), analogous to this same object's existing "body"/"phase" keys) — deliberately v1-scoped to 'title' only; Policy validates the field name/class at manifest-load time and throws on anything else, so slug (which participates in file NAMES and collision/identity checks, not just content) and status/dates/menu_order/comment_status/ping_status/excerpt (no proven self-healing precedent) stay unsupported rather than half-supported. Semantics, argued explicitly since task #88 left both open as valid: Capture keeps writing the field's CURRENT observed value into the file verbatim, every time, exactly like any other front-matter field — never silently omitted, so a human reading state/ always sees what the title actually is right now. Apply's phase-1 insert still writes the captured value as a brand-new row's starting title (no rebuilder exists to conjure one the way _wp_attachment_metadata gets one, and WordPress requires SOME value on insert) — but phase-2 finalize_post() now excludes 'title' from its UPDATE statement entirely once the row exists, rather than overwriting it with the captured byte string on every apply. Chosen over always-write: always-write would make a target environment's own, more-progressed self-heal regress to a stale source snapshot on every apply cycle, only to re-heal itself on the very next ordinary WooCommerce read — a pointless oscillation for a value nothing authored actually controls; letting the plugin's own derivation stand once the row exists is what 'derived' means for a field with no rebuilder. Separately — and this is the half that actually closes the gap rather than relabeling it — Canon::post_hash_basis() excludes every field a post_type classifies derived from the representation that gets HASHED for Ledger's duo_state, Apply::build_plan()'s three-way compare, and Capture::snapshot()'s env view (Capture::run()/snapshot() and Apply::load_tree() all hash this basis now, not the raw file bytes, for posts), so a title-only divergence is structurally invisible to plan/drift/conflict detection, not merely excluded from one test's diff. sandbox/tests/grind_r1b_shop.sh proves both halves on the real Duo Tee fixture: an explicit 'duo plan' assertion that a title-only self-heal on one side alone never appears in drift/update/conflict, and — since capture still records the CURRENT value verbatim, so two environments at genuinely different self-heal moments would still show different file bytes — a forced, real wc_get_product() read (WooCommerce's own natural mechanism, not a duo mechanism, run outside any apply/capture window, the same read any admin product-list view or Store API request triggers naturally) on every variation on both sides before the final byte-identity assertion, which now asserts TRUE identity with the NON_TITLE_DIFFS exclusion removed entirely and passes because both sides converge to the identical WooCommerce-computed value off byte-identical authored inputs.
notes.customer_email: Plain authored string array, NOT a ref:user field. WooCommerce's 'allowed emails' restriction accepts glob patterns (`*@wholesale.example.test`) and arbitrary addresses that need not belong to any registered WP user — that's a merchant-entered business rule, not an identity reference, so it round-trips as opaque strings like _purchase_note rather than through the user-token ref machinery.
notes.coupon_amount / minimum_amount (DUO-3229: The whole-entity scope gate exposed that the Woo conformance site's authored shop_coupon fixture had never entered policy.post_types despite the manifest declaring shop_coupon authored. Once the harness correctly scoped it, lint observed coupon_amount=10 and minimum_amount=10 coinciding with product_variation post id 10. Both values are merchant-entered decimal amount constraints, not identity references; lint_ok is the established audited exemption for this exact small-number coincidence. This is reactive evidence from the real fixture, not a blanket exemption for every numeric coupon key.
notes.date_expires: Single UNIX timestamp (write path: `$value ? $value->getTimestamp() : null` in class-wc-coupon-data-store-cpt.php update_post_meta()) — authored, no ref (an absolute instant, not env-bound). Empirically confirmed on a non-expiring coupon: WooCommerce still writes the postmeta row unconditionally on coupon create, with an actual SQL NULL value (not '', not an absent row) — the common case, since most coupons never expire. Capture round-trips this cleanly as JSON `null`, and apply now writes it back as a real SQL NULL on the target too (Apply::upsert_meta()'s value param was made nullable specifically for this shape — confirmed empirically byte-identical on both sides after the fix landed).
notes.expiry_date: Legacy pre-3.0 predecessor of date_expires, same timestamp shape. WooCommerce's read path only falls back to it when date_expires meta doesn't exist at all (`metadata_exists()` check) — current WC never writes it, but old/migrated/imported coupons can still carry it, and leaving it unclassified would loud-abort capture on exactly the sites most likely to have legacy data.
notes.exclude_product_categories: Same shape as product_categories (see below): ref term[], no cast.
notes.exclude_product_ids: Same shape as product_ids (see below): ref post[], cast csv.
notes.product_categories: Serialized array of real PHP ints (write path: `array_filter(array_map('intval', $value))` then normal maybe_serialize — class-wc-coupon-data-store-cpt.php update_post_meta()), unlike product_ids' CSV-string shape below. ref term[] with no cast — the plain int[] path — confirmed empirically via raw postmeta (`a:1:{i:0;i:19;}`), matching the term_id keyspace (not term_taxonomy_id) that wc_get_product_terms(..., ['fields'=>'ids']) uses elsewhere in WooCommerce.
notes.product_count_* (meta_patterns): Task #122 (found in Grind R3-A): WooCommerce maintains a per-term product-count cache as TERM meta (`product_count_product_cat` observed live on every product_cat term; the taxonomy name rides in the key name, so an exact-key rule can't cover the family) — runtime via meta_patterns, which Policy consults for term_meta and post_meta through the same shared lookup (PATTERN_KEYS maps both sections to meta_patterns). No post-meta collision: WooCommerce writes no product_count_* post meta. R3-A's interim site-policy mitigation (exact-key term_meta rule in its own site.duo.json) is superseded by this entry.
notes.product_ids: Comma-separated string, always (write path: `implode(',', array_filter(array_map('intval', $value)))` in class-wc-coupon-data-store-cpt.php; its own doc-comment notes the read path defensively also accepts a serialized array because 'some plugins mistakenly change these', but WooCommerce itself only ever writes CSV) — ref post[] cast csv, same pattern as _product_image_gallery. Confirmed empirically via raw postmeta (bare digits, e.g. `20`, not a serialized array).
notes.product_visibility: Deliberately NOT added to owned taxonomies (see site.duo.json). Its terms (outofstock, featured, rated-1..5, exclude-from-catalog, exclude-from-search) are partly stock/rating-derived: WooCommerce assigns and removes them itself via its own hooks (e.g. on stock status change) independent of duo, and every environment's WooCommerce activation already creates the full term set. Treating them as owned would fight WooCommerce's own term management for no benefit — products still render and query correctly on a target environment without duo ever touching this taxonomy.
notes.usage_count: Redemption counter, maintained by direct `$wpdb->query('UPDATE ... meta_value = meta_value + 1 ...')` (class-wc-coupon-data-store-cpt.php update_usage_count_meta()) — runtime: it's derived from this environment's own order history, never merchant-authored, and must not be clobbered by a branch's stale count on apply. Confirmed empirically: redeeming a coupon increments it on A; B's independent local value (0, or whatever B's own redemptions produced) must survive apply untouched — see spike_d_woo.sh's coupon section.
notes.attribute_pa_* (meta_patterns): Every USED-FOR-VARIATION global attribute mints a variation-level postmeta key named `attribute_<taxonomy>` (`attribute_pa_size`, `attribute_pa_color`, ...) — the taxonomy name is dynamic (one per merchant-created attribute; see the pa_* note below), so a static post_meta entry can never cover a site's full attribute set, only whichever attributes existed when the manifest was last edited. Confirmed empirically the value is always the term SLUG as a plain string (`small`, `red`) — portable, no numeric id, no ref needed — so `meta_patterns: [{"match": "^attribute_pa_", "class": "authored"}]` covers every past and future global attribute in one declaration with zero risk (the value shape never contains a ref regardless of which attribute the key names). This is the FIRST use of meta_patterns for a genuinely open-ended (not just versioned-suffix) dynamic key family in this manifest set — see the pa_* taxonomies note for why the equivalent taxonomy-name problem has no such escape hatch.
notes.pa_* attribute taxonomies (dynamic taxon: SUPERSEDED by task #92's taxonomy_patterns entry below — this note is kept verbatim as the empirical trail that motivated it, not deleted (this project's convention: append, don't erase history). WooCommerce mints a taxonomy per global attribute at runtime — `wc_attribute_taxonomy_name()` returns `'pa_' . sanitize_title($attribute->attribute_name)` (truncated+hashed past 27 chars) — registered on `init` by reading `wp_woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies` (a custom table, see the tables section below), NOT declared anywhere in code. This manifest cannot list pa_size/pa_color the way manifests/core.json lists category/post_tag: every NEW global attribute a merchant creates is a taxonomy this manifest has never heard of. Confirmed empirically what actually happens: (1) TERM data (the taxonomy's own terms — Small/Medium/Large, Red/Blue/Black — and a product's term_relationships under that taxonomy) flows through the EXISTING generic taxonomy-capture machinery with ZERO new engine code, exactly like category/product_cat, the moment the taxonomy's bare name is added to site.duo.json's policy.taxonomies array — proving the generic terms path is genuinely attribute-agnostic. (2) Policy::taxonomies() (agent/src/Policy.php) returns that array as a flat, exact-string list with NO pattern/wildcard fallback — unlike options and post_meta/term_meta, taxonomies has no PATTERN_KEYS entry at all (confirmed by reading Policy::rule()'s pattern-fallback code, which is keyed off a fixed PATTERN_KEYS map that only has 'options' and 'post_meta'/'term_meta'). So while attribute_pa_* POST META was solvable with one meta_patterns line (see above), the TAXONOMY SCOPE LIST has no equivalent: every new global attribute needs a manual, human site.duo.json edit adding its exact pa_<name> string, forever — there is no manifest-level fix available in this engine for taxonomies the way there is for meta keys. (3) The sharper failure is on the TARGET environment, not the source: pa_size/pa_color's very existence as registered taxonomies depends on rows in the woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies custom table, which nothing in this engine captures or applies (see the tables note) — so on a fresh environment that has never had that attribute created through its own admin/wp-cli, `get_taxonomy('pa_size')` returns false. Capture.php's own taxes_by_object_type() already anticipates exactly this ('a scoped taxonomy that isn't registered at runtime... is excluded entirely and named in a loud warning') for the CAPTURE side; empirically, applying pa_size/pa_color TERM entities via `duo apply` on such an environment is the sharper, unguarded case — term insertion itself calls WordPress's own wp_insert_term()/taxonomy APIs, which behave unpredictably (silently registering an ad hoc, config-less taxonomy row, or failing) against a taxonomy WooCommerce itself doesn't know exists yet, because nothing upstream of that call ever re-created the woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies row that would have registered it for real. The empirically-verified, honest mitigation for this grind round: PRE-PROVISION every global attribute (`wp wc product_attribute create` — the same real, admin-facing action used to create it originally) on every target environment BEFORE the first apply that references its terms, exactly the same operational discipline this sandbox already uses for WooCommerce/Storefront themselves (installed independently on both environments, never propagated through the site repo's code/ tree). This is a manual step, not an automated one — see docs/grind/r1b-shop.md for the acceptance criteria a real typed-snapshot implementation for woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies would need to remove it.
notes.taxonomy_patterns (task #92, closes the: Two mechanisms compose to close zero-provisioning: task #75's woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies typed-snapshot (already shipped) makes the ATTRIBUTE TABLE ROW itself travel — confirmed live by r3-eng-fields validating #88 on r1b2: right after a `duo apply` that lands a new attribute row, `get_taxonomy('pa_size')`/`get_taxonomy('pa_color')` both return true in the NEXT fresh wp-cli process, zero manual steps. What #75 alone does NOT fix is (a) the taxonomy SCOPE LIST (site.duo.json still needed pa_size/pa_color listed by hand — Policy::taxonomies() had no pattern fallback) and (b) relationship-writing correctness WITHIN the SAME apply request that lands a brand-new attribute (WooCommerce registers pa_* taxonomies by reading its table on `init`, which already ran before Snapshot's phase-1 write of that table's row this request — reproduced directly, not just reasoned about: a raw-SQL insert into wp_woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies leaves get_taxonomy() returning false for the REST of that same PHP process, even though a paired raw-SQL term_taxonomy row for the new taxonomy name is immediately visible to a live `SELECT DISTINCT taxonomy FROM wp_term_taxonomy` in the identical process). taxonomy_patterns closes both: Policy::taxonomies() now expands the exact policy.taxonomies list with every live wp_term_taxonomy name matching a declared pattern (scope-gated — never a blanket widen, only pattern-matched names are ever added), and the declared `object_type` here is consulted ONLY as a fallback when get_taxonomy() fails, letting direct-SQL term-relationship writes correctly scope a just-landed pa_* taxonomy without needing WordPress's runtime registry to have caught up. `object_type: ["product"]` is sourced from WooCommerce's actual current code (fetched directly, not recalled): class-wc-post-types.php's register_taxonomies() calls `register_taxonomy($name, apply_filters("woocommerce_taxonomy_objects_{$name}", array('product')), ...)` — the literal, unfiltered default for every pa_* taxonomy. With both mechanisms in place, site.duo.json no longer needs pa_size/pa_color listed at all — the whole point of zero manual provisioning.
notes.shipping zones & tax rates (task #93, GR:
All five tables (woocommerce_shipping_zones/zone_locations/zone_methods, woocommerce_tax_rates/tax_rate_locations) DESCRIBE'd fresh for this task, confirming the earlier note's shapes still hold on this install. Identity mode: `mapped` for ALL FIVE (not natural_key for any), a genuinely different outcome than woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies — argued and CONFIRMED against WooCommerce's own current source (fetched class-wc-shipping-zone.php directly, not recalled): WC_Shipping_Zone::save() has no uniqueness check on zone_name at all, only a default-name fill-in when one is missing; re-confirmed live via the real wc-cli path (`wp wc shipping_zone create`) — two zones named 'Duplicate Test' were created cleanly with different zone_ids, no rejection. zone_location/zone_method/tax_rate_location natural-key candidates (location_code, method_id) all fail too: they're scoped WITHIN a parent (a zone/rate), not globally unique — location_code='US' recurs across every zone targeting the US, so treating it as a natural key would derive the IDENTICAL uuid for every such zone's location row; Snapshot.php's grammar has no composite-key support to fix this even if it wanted to (filed as task #125, a genuine follow-on gap, not blocking this task). Topology: both parent/child clusters (zones -> {locations, methods}; tax_rates -> {tax_rate_locations}) are single-parent, direct-children only — the identical shape nf3_forms -> {nf3_fields, nf3_actions} already proved; Snapshot.php needed ZERO code changes beyond the task #93-required Snapshot::row_exists_for_kind() helper (for option_name_refs' dangling-vs-unscoped distinction, argued below) — ownership was allocated, not a quota to fill. Caching, sourced from WooCommerce's actual code (fetched directly, both files): WC_Shipping_Zones::get_zones() has NO cache wrapping it at all (only the narrower get_zone_matching_package() caches) — confirmed live, a raw-SQL-inserted zone+method was visible via get_zones() from a SEPARATE wp-cli process with zero explicit invalidation. WC_Tax::find_rates() DOES cache (object-cache group 'taxes', keyed by location+class, via direct wp_cache_get()/wp_cache_set() — NOT get_transient(), a materially different, request-scoped-only mechanism absent a persistent object-cache backend) — confirmed live via wp_using_ext_object_cache() that no persistent backend is active in this sandbox, and confirmed a raw-SQL-inserted tax rate was visible via find_rates() from a separate process with zero invalidation. Net: no rebuilder needed for either table family in this environment; flagged explicitly (not silently assumed) that a site running a real persistent object-cache plugin would need one for tax rates specifically — a documented, not-yet-hit edge case.

THE OPTION-NAME MECHANISM (option_name_refs, closing the third compounding problem the note above named): a new manifest section, sibling to option_patterns (not nested inside `tables` — every other section is an independently-mergeable top-level sibling; nesting would be the only cross-section nesting in the whole grammar and would misplace the concept, since an option's relationship to an id_kind is the same shape as an ordinary `options` ref rule's relationship to the post/term keyspace). `match` is a regex with a required named group `id` marking the ref-bearing segment — anchored `^...$`, tested live against real option names on this install including two genuine false-positive risks (woocommerce_paypal_settings, woocommerce_maxmind_geolocation_settings, both matching a naive `*_settings` search but correctly EXCLUDED by this regex since neither ends in a digit run before `_settings`). Capture::build_options() runs one full option-NAME scan (names only) per capture and tests each against every declared pattern — a new discovery mechanism, since Policy::authored_options() is exact-whitelist-only and never consults option_patterns for discovery at all (confirmed by reading it directly, and matches this task's own prior characterization). The captured KEY splices the resolved ref TOKEN into the id segment's exact byte position (e.g. `woocommerce_flat_rate_{{wc_zone_method:<uuid>}}_settings`) using the SAME `{{kind:uuid}}` grammar every other ref already uses — Tokens::id_to_token()/token_to_id() needed zero changes, confirmed already generic over any declared id_kind. Apply detects a token-bearing option KEY before its ordinary option-rule dispatch (unconditionally, not gated) — confirmed this ordering is load-bearing, not cosmetic: skipping it would silently write a REAL wp_options row whose NAME contains literal '{{...}}' bytes to the target, not a crash. Severity model (team-lead design review, mirroring task #73's dangling-vs-unscoped split): an embedded id resolving to no row anywhere is ordinary dangling (warn+drop); an embedded id naming a row that genuinely EXISTS in its declared table but was never minted a uuid (e.g. the table isn't pinned as authored_snapshot) is unscoped (loud, blocking, `--force-unresolved-refs` escape hatch — Snapshot::row_exists_for_kind() is the new helper this distinction needed). Settings VALUES route through struct_capture()/struct_apply() unconditionally (not gated on json_refs/key_refs being declared, unlike ordinary options) specifically so an array-shaped settings blob (title/cost/tax_status for flat_rate; title/min_amount for free_shipping — both confirmed live, plain scalars, no ids) gets its string leaves URL-tokenized with zero per-method-id special-casing; deliberately NOT the same default as ordinary build_options() (which leaves an untouched array value alone unless json_refs/key_refs is declared) — this is a new, narrower path scoped only to option_name_refs rows, so it doesn't risk a behavior change to already-shipped manifests. Secret guard: Secrets::hard_match_deep() (not the shallow is_string() check the ordinary options loop uses, which would silently never scan an array's own string leaves — caught during this task's own design review before any code shipped, before it could become a real gap) — verified live against both real fixtures (flat_rate, free_shipping settings, both null/clean) AND a deliberately-planted fake Stripe key nested in the same array shape (correctly caught), proving the guard actually works.
notes.woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies (task #: Re-DESCRIBE'd live for this task, not reused from the R1-B report's summary alone (though it confirms that report byte-for-byte): attribute_id (bigint PK auto_increment), attribute_name (varchar(200), a plain non-unique-constrained MUL index at the DB level — but WooCommerce's OWN admin/wc-cli create path refuses a duplicate name at the application layer, which is what makes it a genuinely stable, human-chosen natural key in practice, per docs/grind/r1b-shop.md's finding), attribute_label/attribute_type/attribute_orderby/attribute_public (plain scalars, no ids anywhere). Zero FK-shaped columns — the simplest possible authored_snapshot fixture, deliberately chosen as this task's SECONDARY proof precisely because it stresses the OTHER half of the typed-snapshot design (identity.mode=natural_key, a table with no _duo_uuid-equivalent AND no FK to resolve) that nf3_forms's mapped-identity, FK-bearing shape doesn't exercise. Uuid::v5(Uuid::NAMESPACE_DUO, "woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies:<attribute_name>") mints a uuid deterministically from the name alone — re-derivable even after a full duo_map loss, closing exactly the manual pre-provisioning gap docs/grind/r1b-shop.md's own acceptance criteria named ('zero manual pre-provisioning step'): applying a captured pa_size/pa_color definition to a target that has never seen it creates the woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies row for real (through Snapshot.php's phase-1/phase-2 insert), which is what makes pa_size/pa_color get_taxonomy()-registered on init without a human running `wp wc product_attribute create` by hand first. The wc_attribute_taxonomies TRANSIENT cache hazard (docs/grind/r1b-shop.md: surviving a raw table write, causing a real 'slug already in use' error against an empty table) is closed by the top-level `rebuilders` entry above (`transient delete wc_attribute_taxonomies`, WooCommerce's own cache key, confirmed by that report) — a BLANKET, not row-id-keyed, invalidation, unlike nf3_upgrades' per-form cache, so the pre-existing rebuilders mechanism covers it with zero new engine code (see manifests/ninja-forms.json's note for the row-id-keyed case Snapshot.php's `invalidate` mechanism exists for instead). Term DATA (pa_size/pa_color's own Small/Medium/Large etc.) still round-trips through the pre-existing generic taxonomy machinery, unchanged — this note is only about the CUSTOM TABLE that registers the taxonomy for real, closing the 'sharper failure is on the target' finding docs/grind/r1b-shop.md documented. `attribute_public` is declared `lint_ok: true`: a 0/1 boolean flag, confirmed live to trip wp duo lint's bare_id check against this fixture's own placeholder attachment (post id 1) the first time this was wired end-to-end — the same 'reviewed, genuinely not a ref' exemption as this manifest's own `queryId` entry above and ninja-forms.json's BIT(1) columns.
notes.shipping zones & tax rates (custom table: Kept verbatim as the empirical trail that motivated task #93 (this project's convention: append, don't erase history) — see the task #93 note for the real, shipped grammar. wc_shipping_zones/wc_shipping_zone_locations/wc_shipping_zone_methods and wc_tax_rates/wc_tax_rate_locations hold 100% of a shop's shipping-zone and tax-rate configuration — real merchant-authored business rules with zero post/option representation. Stated plainly, verified by reading the engine, not assumed: Capture.php has NO code path that reads ANY custom table into canonical state, for ANY manifest, ever — `Policy::table_rule()` (the only consumer of a manifest's "tables" section) is called exactly once in this codebase, from Journal.php's ground_truth(), purely to score provenance-journal proposals ('managed', i.e. deliberately-out-of-scope, rather than 'unclassified'). It has no effect whatsoever on what `duo capture`/`duo apply` do. So every table below is added to this manifest as an intent marker only — the same honest, no-implementation-behind-it convention manifests/woocommerce.json already established for woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies before this round touched it — NOT a claim of coverage. Empirically characterized column shapes (DESCRIBE against a live WooCommerce 11.0.0 install), precise enough to write the eventual typed-snapshot acceptance criteria from: `wc_shipping_zones` (zone_id PK auto_increment, zone_name, zone_order — no FK-shaped columns of its own, but IS a referenced parent: zone_id is a natural candidate for its own ledger id_kind since two child tables point at it) / `wc_shipping_zone_locations` (location_id PK, zone_id FK -> shipping_zones, location_code a semantic string like 'US' or 'US:CA' — not a ref, location_type) / `wc_shipping_zone_methods` (zone_id FK, instance_id PK auto_increment, method_id a plain string like 'flat_rate'/'free_shipping', method_order, is_enabled). `wc_tax_rates` (tax_rate_id PK auto_increment — a referenced parent for one child table, no FK columns of its own — tax_rate_country/state/rate/name/priority/compound/shipping/order/class, all plain scalars) / `wc_tax_rate_locations` (location_id PK, tax_rate_id FK -> tax_rates, location_code, location_type). The genuinely novel sub-problem, sharper than 'declare column-level refs on a custom table' (DESIGN.md's own framing for typed snapshot): shipping METHOD instance SETTINGS (title/cost/tax_status for flat_rate; min_amount for free_shipping) are NOT columns on wc_shipping_zone_methods at all — they live in `wp_options`, under a name the method instance's own auto-increment id is baked into: `woocommerce_<method_id>_<instance_id>_settings` (confirmed empirically live: creating a flat_rate method on a fresh zone minted `woocommerce_flat_rate_1_settings`; a free_shipping method on the same zone minted `woocommerce_free_shipping_2_settings` — instance_id 1 and 2, this environment's own auto-increment sequence). Three compounding problems, not one: (a) the option's NAME, not just its value, contains an environment-local id, so no `ref`-on-value declaration (the only kind this manifest format has) can fix it; (b) that id is minted by an entirely different table's auto-increment counter, so resolving it needs a ledger lookup keyed by a DIFFERENT entity's identity, a cross-table dependency no current option rule can express; (c) `options` capture is whitelist-only by exact key (`Policy::authored_options()`, read by `Capture::build_options()`) with NO pattern-matching path at all, confirmed by reading the function directly — unlike `attribute_pa_*` above, `option_patterns` exists as a manifest key and IS consulted by `Policy::option_rule()`, but `authored_options()` never calls it, so even a matching option_patterns rule would never cause `build_options()` to discover and read the row; the instance id being unpredictable in advance (it's minted per zone/method, per environment, in creation order) means there is no fixed option NAME a static rule could list either. This shape needs new engine capability on three axes at once (id-in-option-name resolution, cross-table ledger dependency, and a discovery mechanism replacing the exact-key whitelist) before it can even become a manifest-authoring problem — not attempted here; characterized instead so the acceptance criteria in docs/grind/r1b-shop.md are grounded in what was actually found, not guessed.
